name: Kilburn Engineering Ltd
tagline: Industrial drying / process-equipment maker (rotary & paddle dryers, calciners, WHR, RF drying) that grew ~50% in FY26 at a 25%+ EBITDA margin and has just opened a US/EU OEM-manufacturing vector (Komline exclusive, first Casale export order) - but Q1 FY27 revenue fell 8.5% YoY after 50%/25% growth guidance, consolidated cash flow has been chronically negative, equity is serially diluted, and the Khaitan promoter group carries a documented capital-allocation history
business_overview: Kilburn makes industrial drying and process equipment - rotary and paddle dryers, calciners, heat exchangers, tea-drying equipment, titanium equipment for defence - for chemicals, fertilizer, pharma, metals and food customers, and has moved toward being a 'solution provider'. Growth has been acquisition-assisted: ME Energy (waste-heat recovery), Monga Strayfield (RF drying), and an Ambernath factory. It has a Definitive/Master Agreement with Komline-Sanderson (New Jersey) to exclusively manufacture turbo and paddle dryers for them, and a first-ever ~Rs 70.2 Cr export order from Casale SA (Switzerland). Promoter group is the Khaitan family (~22-23%) plus Firstview Investments / the OCCL (Oriental Carbon / Goenka) group (~35%); professionally managed. Listed on NSE from April 2026 (was BSE-only). Sovrenn Daily News seed (2026-09-02); Sovrenn trigger: the Casale first export order.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 643 Cr (+~50% YoY); EBITDA margin stepped 22% -> ~26% (two-plus quarters at 25%+)
Revenue ~Rs 120.5 Cr (-8.5% YoY); EBITDA ~Rs 24.2 Cr (20.1% margin, down from ~27%); PAT ~Rs 13.1 Cr (from ~Rs 21.3 Cr) - a clear miss
~Rs 492 Cr backlog; ~Rs 4,000 Cr bid pipeline at ~20-25% historical conversion
Guided ~50% growth for FY26 then ~25% CAGR, 22-23% EBITDA - Q1 FY27 undershoot on 'slower conversions'
Net-debt-free as of 30-Jun-2026; credit rating upgraded to A. But consolidated CFFO has been negative for years (debtor + unbilled-revenue build on long-delivery projects)
Komline-Sanderson (US) exclusive manufacturing tie-up for turbo/paddle dryers; first-ever ~Rs 70.2 Cr Casale SA (Switzerland) export order; nuclear-power order inflow noted
fundamentals_narrative: Kilburn is a niche capital-goods compounder with a genuine new leg - exclusive OEM manufacturing for Komline (US) and a first export order from Casale (Switzerland) - on top of FY26 revenue +50% at a 25%+ EBITDA margin and a Rs 4,000 Cr bid pipeline. But three things temper it. First, execution just missed: Q1 FY27 revenue was down 8.5% YoY on 'slower conversions' after management guided 50% then 25% growth (guidance_credibility over-promises). Second, consolidated operating cash flow has been chronically negative for years as debtors and unbilled revenue build on long-delivery projects, and equity has been serially diluted (~17-18% in FY23-24, then ~Rs 300 Cr of warrants, then Monga) so EPS lags PAT. Third, the Khaitan promoter family has a documented capital-allocation history at other group companies - McLeod Russel defaulted and wrote off ~Rs 900 Cr of group-company loans in FY23 with the stock down ~99% from its peak, Eveready struggled with leverage, and there is a board-level family dispute (Aditya vs Amritanshu Khaitan, both on Kilburn's board). Mitigants: Kilburn itself is low-debt, the larger holder is the non-family OCCL/Goenka strategic investor, and day-to-day management is professional.
